title: Exhaustive by Design
goal: Cover the last status - in the way that keeps future variants loud.
hints: The wildcard works today. Now imagine adding Status::Suspended next month - which version tells you every place to update?
Name the variant. Exhaustiveness checking is the feature; _ turns it off.
explanation: Both Status::Banned and _ compile, pass, and rank equally here - Rust cannot measure future-proofing. The difference appears next month: with named variants, adding Status::Suspended makes every match a compile error listing exactly what to update; the wildcard swallows new variants silently - 'blocked' forever, wrongly. (Status::Blocked doesn't exist; the compiler catches pattern typos too, E0599.) Prefer naming what you handle; treat _ as a deliberate decision, not a habit.
